patch_description: The dominant scoring weakness is slope churn (slope_changes=167.8, false_reversals=127.4) while accuracy is already high. The best prior program (combined 0.58) achieved slope_changes=41 and false_reversals=36 via implicit slope damping (Kalman velocity state + Savitzky-Golay). I port that mechanism into this pipeline as an explicit, cheap "trend-lock" stage: the leading-edge fit already computes per-window slopes; I return them, then apply EMA shrinkage-smoothing of the slope sequence and adjust the output level by the slope disagreement. Because the level estimate y[i] is already evaluated at the window's leading edge (zero group delay), this damping adds almost no lag (lag_error stays ~0.3) while suppressing noise-induced directional reversals — exactly the trade the best prior program exploited. Additionally, I tighten Stage 3 slightly (k 0.5→0.65) since the trend-lock stage will do most of the reversal killing. All stages remain vectorized/O(n), preserving efficiency_score=1.0.
